text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a move that renewed speculation that Kerry Packer was looking into a bid for either Sydney Harbour Casino Ltd or newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings, Packer surprised the market by selling almost two-thirds of his stake in Melbourne's A$1.6 billion Crown casino for A$204 million. Page 1.

In meetings in Tokyo over the next two days, Prime Minister John Howard is expected to call on a reluctant Japan to lead the region in opening new markets as the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation (APEC) trade liberalisation process approaches an important test of credibility - the APEC leaders' summit in November. Page 1.

Prime Minister Howard's comments to an Indonesia Australia Business Council lunch suggesting Australia's political institutions will soon go through important changes were welcomed by the business audience members who had been concerned that a new Australian government would upset the carefully nurtured business relationship of the past few years. Page 3.

David Jones chief executive Chris Tideman said yesterday the upmarket retailer had seen no signs of an upturn in soft trading conditions in the past month and said the group was continuing to feel the impact of flagging consumer confidence, with a disappinting first-half result for 1996/97 foreshadowed. Page 19.

Australian life companies, including National Mutual and Legal & General, are fearful the Thai government could review a proposal to approve up to 66 new life and non-life companies ahead of this week's parliamentary vote of no confidence against Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa. Page 21.

In a filing with the Australian Stock Exchange yesterday, Australis Media Ltd revealed that it had suffered further massive customer losses because of its financial crisis, with subscriber numbers plummeting over the past year. About 48 percent of its subscrber base has quit the service in the six months to August. Page 21.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics yesterday forecast a seven percent jump in mineral and energy exports in 1996/97 based on strengthening global demand and a continuing domestic investment boom. The mining and resources sector looks set to see a A$37 billion export bonanza in that period. Page 39.

In a negative assessment of the retail outlook, David Jones Ltd said sales in August were as difficult as in the fourth quarter and the upmarket retailer refused to predict an improvement in earnings for the current financial year after falling short of most of its prospectus forecasts. Page 39.

Kerry Packer's Consolidated Press Holdings Ltd has made a profit of A$120 million on the sale of its holding in Melbourne casino operator Crown Ltd - 75 million shares or 15 percent of Crown at A$2.72 a share - through BZW Corporate Finance. CPH raised atotal of A$204 million yesterday from the sale. Page 39.

Thanks to an innovation by Brazilian telecommunications service provider Itacomp Industria, which allows one phone line to be used for up to 32 simultaneous calls, Australian company Intellect Holdings Ltd, which sells technology linking its customers to banks via phone lines, has overcome the difficulty of selling modern technology to a country with a Third World phone system. Page 39.

Following the merger with the Queensland Queensco United co-operative, The Dairy Farmers Group, Australia's largest dairy co-operative, remains confident of another positive performance this financial year after yesterday announcing a nine percent rise in net profit to A$25.4 million for the year. Page 41.

There are increasing concerns for the outlook of BHP after analysts factored in production results last night for the three months to August, which point to continuing difficulties for the steel division and persisting softness in the global copper market. BHP's shares price saw the effects of nervous investors, falling 48 cents to A$16. Page 41.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Kerry Packer's Consolidated Press Holdings has raised A$204 million by selling its 15 percent stake in Melbourne's Crown casino, giving Consolidated Press the capacity of investing up to A$1 billion for expansion. Analysts claim the group's next big acqusition is likely to be in the media or entertainment area. Page 27.

Property and development group Lend Lease Corp is to spend A$50 million on its first property development in Indonesia, near Jakarta. The 11.3-hectare development at Cempaka Putih is a A$200 million mixed-use project in which Lend Lease will receive 50 percent equity for A$50 million. Page 29.

Market analysts are expecting BHP to report a first-quarter profit on Friday about 10 percent down on last year, despite the group's increased production. The mining giant is tipped to report a net result of about A$330 million for the three months against A$372 million a year earlier. Page 27.

Australia's largest institutional agricultural investors have added to claims that New South Wales' booming agricultural exports are under threat from the state government's water policies. New South Wales irrigators reliant on the Murray Darling Basin suply are being undermined by a state government agreement which reduces the allocation of water for farmers, whilst Victoria, Queensland and South Australia further develop their irrigation sectors. Page 29.

Resolute Samantha has been finishing-off the final touches of a A$150 million share placement aimed at funding development of three new projects and continuing its exploration programmes. The new shares represent a 30 percent increase in the Perth-based mining group's capital base. Page 29.

Bill Zimmerman, BHP's diamond marketing manager, believes there is a 50 percent chance the group would sell diamonds from it's Lac de Gras project in Canada outside of the Central Selling Organisation. Zimmerman said BHP is yet to finalise the decision, but BHP believes the high quality of its diamonds will mean they will be in strong demand. Page 30.
THE AGE

Media magnate Kerry Packer yesterday off-loaded a 15 percent stake in Melbourne's Crown casino for more than A$200 million, fuelling rumours that he is preparing for a possible bid for the newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings. In a statement to the Australian Stock Exchange, Crown confirmed the sale of Packer's 75 million shares at A$2.72/share. Page C1.

Retail giant and recently floated David Jones has reported slightly better margins than last financial year and lower-than-expected costs in the year to 27 July. Sales reached A$1.44 billion, and although slightly ahead of 1994/95, fell 5.7 percent short of forecasts. Profits before interest and tax for retail operations were A$67.3 million. Page C1.

According to an Australian business confidence survey conducted by Westpac Banking Corporation and the Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, business confidence increased in the two weeks following the 20 August budget, although it remained below confidence levels recorded after the March 2 election when the Coalition won government. Page C3.

The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics has forecast the Australian minerals and energy sector will enjoy the best year yet with an estimated A$37 billion in exports. Meanwhile, total farming sector production is expected to fall slightly to A$26.3 billion, down 3.3 percent from the 1995/96 year. Page C3.

The continuing hard-times in the retail sector have shown in the fashion and homewares retailer Country Road which has produced a flat operating profit of A$10.2 million for the year ended 28 July. This figure is up 0.3 percent on last year's and Country Road's earnings per share fell to 16.6 cents from 28.5 cents during the same period. Page C1.

A New South Wales commission of inquiry has approved a A$380 million, 740 km underground gas pipeline to be built between New South Wales and Victoria in a joint venture between BHP Petroleum and West-Coast Energy Australia. The pipeline will transfer Bass Strait gas between the south-east of Victoria to a point south of Sydney. Page C5.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
